At the low deformation temperature (900–950 °C) and high strain rate (1–10 s^-1) regime, the DRX grains are small but DRX is not sufficient and large-sized original grains remain, giving poor microstructural homogeneity. The measured grain size is taken from the core of the compressed sample (large deformation zone).

This sample (900 °C, 1 s^-1) falls in that regime.

unmapped_findings: lnZ for this sample (T = 900 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1) is 68.69 (Table 1); lnZ increases with increasing strain rate and decreasing temperature, so this condition lies at the high-Z (harder-to-recrystallize) end of the experimental matrix.

The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material: rheological stress increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T; peak stress can be lowered by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0084).
The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ·mol^-1 (b0012, b0085).

Peak stress for the specific 900 °C/1 s^-1 condition is not tabulated in the text; from the 3D peak-stress map for ε̇ = 1–10 s^-1 (Fig. 3d, colour bar 94.00–486.0 MPa) the 900 °C region is at the high end of the scale (b0024, figure_003). At 900 °C the peak stress at 0.01 s^-1 was 305.4 MPa (b0024), and at 1150 °C it fell to 53.8 MPa at 0.01 s^-1 (82% reduction) and by 73% at 10 s^-1.

Optimal hot-working conditions for a fine and uniform grain structure are 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086). This sample (900 °C/1 s^-1) lies outside these windows.
At low T (900–950 °C) and high ε̇ (1–10 s^-1) the DRX grains are small but DRX is insufficient and large original grains remain, giving poor microstructure homogeneity (b0063).
According to the DRX state diagram (Fig. 7), as lnZ increases the critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs both increase, i.e. starting and completing DRX becomes more difficult (b0058).

The experimental results (including reproducibility, checked by repeating isothermal compression on the same steel batch under identical conditions) were stated to be reproducible (b0018, b0024, b0037, b0065).
The initial (pre-deformation) microstructure consists of large polygonal grains with fine parallel striations (segregation/dendritic banding) and no numeric grain size is reported (figure_001).
